title: GS The Fresh Becomes First in Industry to Reach 500 Franchise Stores - 아시아경제
content:
GS The Fresh Becomes First in Industry to Reach 500 Franchise Stores GS The Fresh, the supermarket chain operated by GS Retail, has become the first in the industry to reach 500 franchise stores. On August 20, GS The Fresh announced the opening of its 500th franchise store, the 'GS The Fresh Songpa Seokchon Station branch,' in Seokchon-dong, Songpa-gu, Seoul. With this new location, the total number of GS The Fresh stores has increased to 603. The GS The Fresh Songpa Seokchon Station branch occupies a dedicated area of 288 square meters (87.5 pyeong) along Songpa-daero. The store's products and services are tailored to meet the daily shopping needs of newlyweds and families residing in nearby residential areas. The opening ceremony was attended by key personnel including franchise owner Oh Byungsang, GS Retail CEO Heo Seohong, and GS Retail Super BU Head Kwak Yonggu, among others. A front view image of GS The Fresh Songpa Seokchon Station store, opened as the 500th franchise location. GS The Fresh GS The Fresh, which traces its roots back to the 'Lucky Super Chain' launched in 1974, has grown into a supermarket brand visited by approximately 150 million people annually. Since opening its first franchise, the Sinsa branch, in 2010, the company has reached the milestone of 500 franchise stores in just 16 years. The operation of franchise stores has been supported by a chain operation system. By standardizing the product selection and having headquarters take the lead in display and ordering, the burden on franchise owners has been reduced. This has enabled each store to focus on marketing and business promotion activities tailored to their local customer base. Notably, in 2020, the year after the full-scale introduction of the chain operation system, the proportion of franchise stores surpassed 50% for the first time, and it currently stands at around 83%. Additional revenue opportunities for franchise stores are also being explored through quick commerce. GS The Fresh is strengthening its one-hour shopping delivery service by integrating with various channels, including the GS Neighborhood App, Baedal Minjok, Coupang Eats, Yogiyo, and Naver Shopping. Currently, the quick commerce service is available at most GS The Fresh stores nationwide. In the first half of this year, quick commerce sales at GS The Fresh increased by 41.9% compared to the same period last year. In the second quarter, quick commerce accounted for 9.9% of total sales, the highest proportion to date. At the same time, GS The Fresh is expanding franchise openings in prime locations based on GIS (Geographic Information System) market analysis, and is optimizing product mix and operations at existing stores using store-by-store market and customer data, thereby driving comparable store sales growth. From January to July of this year, GS The Fresh recorded a comparable store sales growth rate of 6.2% year-on-year. Kwak Yonggu, Head of the Super BU at GS Retail, stated, "GS The Fresh is quickly increasing its number of stores by shifting its business structure to focus on franchises and by actively seeking new revenue opportunities, such as quick commerce." He added, "Through AX and data-driven management, we will enhance franchise competitiveness and operational efficiency, aiming for shared growth and stable profitability for franchise owners." © The Asia Business Daily. The chain operation system also supported stable operations at franchise stores. It standardized product assortments and had headquarters handle merchandising and ordering to reduce operators' burdens, allowing franchisees to focus on marketing and sales suited to their trade areas. In 2020, the year after full-scale adoption of chain operation, the share of franchises among all stores surpassed 50% for the first time, and it is now about 83%. It is also expanding its quick commerce business. Along with its own application, Our Neighborhood GS app, it offers grocery delivery within one hour in connection with Baemin, Coupang Eats, Yogiyo, and Naver Shopping. In the first half of this year, GS The Fresh's quick commerce sales rose 41.9% from a year earlier. In the second quarter, quick commerce accounted for 9.9% of total sales, the highest on record. GS The Fresh is applying trade-area analysis using a geographic information system (GIS) to new openings, and it is also optimizing product assortments and store operations based on store-by-store trade areas and customer data. From January to July this year, same-store sales increased 6.2% from a year earlier. Kwak Yong-gu, head of the Super BU at GS Retail, said, "We are expanding the number of stores by shifting to a franchise-centered business structure and are also finding additional revenue opportunities such as quick commerce," and added, "Through AX and data-based management, we will enhance franchise competitiveness and operational efficiency and grow together with store operators." [Click e-Stock] "Strong Results and New Business Potential" GS Target Price Raised DB Financial Investment raised its target price for GS from 1.2 million won to 1.5 million won. This upward adjustment reflects both the company’s second-quarter operating profit, which far exceeded market expectations, and strong anticipation for future new business growth. On August 20, DB Financial Investment stated in its GS corporate analysis report titled "Everything Will Be Fine" that, “As GS has made the most attractive growth investment by leveraging its portfolio, expectations for a re-rating (stock price re-evaluation) will rise further.” Along with the increase in target price, the investment opinion remains ‘Buy.’ The previous day’s closing price for GS was 1,197,000 won. Previously released second-quarter operating profit for GS was 1.7 trillion won, far exceeding the market consensus of 1.1 trillion won. In particular, GS Caltex posted record-breaking results on the back of improved refining margins, driving the overall performance. GS Caltex’s second-quarter operating profit reached 2.55 trillion won, and net profit came to 1.86 trillion won, both all-time highs. As refining margins improved, profitability in the refining division rose sharply. Strong results are expected for GS Caltex in the third quarter as well. Han Seungjae, a research analyst at DB Financial Investment, stated, “Assuming the average price of Dubai crude oil in the third quarter is 79 dollars per barrel, GS Caltex’s estimated inventory valuation loss will be about 1 trillion won.” However, Han added, “With continued strength in refining margins, refining operating profit is expected to reach 950 billion won, supporting robust quarterly results.” The analyst further noted, “The strong performance in lubricants also continues,” forecasting total third-quarter operating profit for GS Caltex to reach 1.38 trillion won. He also pointed out that for the shortage of refining supply to be resolved, several factors are required: normalization of the Strait of Hormuz, comprehensive crude oil export approvals from China, and expanded domestic consumption. However, these conditions have yet to materialize. Entering the peak season, together with a rebound in System Marginal Price (SMP), DB Financial Investment also projected that the combined operating profit of the three power generation subsidiaries will rebound as well. DB Financial Investment assessed that it is now time for GS to use the significant cash flow it secured during the boom period to invest in new businesses. Since the mixed feed cracker (MFC) facility, which received an investment of 2.7 trillion won, began operations in 2022, GS’s capital expenditure (CAPEX) has declined, while this year, GS Caltex’s earnings strength is projected to hit an all-time high. Particular attention was given to GS’s initiatives for artificial intelligence data center (AIDC) projects based on its power generation businesses. The analyst said, “It is now time to deploy massive earnings into new ventures,” emphasizing that, “as progress is made in securing permits and engaging tenant negotiations, expectations for AIDC growth will increase.” © The Asia Business Daily. title: Karol G Floods Hot Latin Songs Chart With ‘No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto’ - Billboard
content: Judeline and Rusowsky score a breakthrough with "BbY WOW," the highest charting collab by a Latin act. Sr. Charts & Data Analyst (Latin & Billboard Español) It’s a big week for Karol G on the Billboard charts. Her sixth studio album, No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto, becomes her fifth No. 1 on Top Latin Albums, while its tracks storm Hot Latin Songs, Hot Latin Pop Songs, Hot Latin Rhythm Songs and Hot Regional Mexican Songs charts (dated Aug. 22). Starting with Hot Latin Songs, Karol pushes Bad Bunny’s “DTMF” down to No. 2. The latter has spent 72 nonconsecutive weeks at No. 1 since its first week on top in January 2025. That 72-week haul stands as the longest command in the history of the nearly 40-year-old tally, which mixes streaming activity, radio airplay and digital sales into its formula. Fueled by streaming activity, Karol G’s “Ahí,” with Drake, bows at No. 1 after registering 5.9 million official on-demand streams in the United States during the tracking week ending Aug. 13, according to Luminate. That sum sends the song to a No. 46 start on the overall Streaming Songs chart and to No. 1 on Latin Streaming Songs. “Ahí” puts Karol G and Drake back on top of Hot Latin Songs — more than two years after their last reigns. Karol’s “Si Antes Te Hubiera Conocido” matched the chart’s longest run of 2024, ruling for 14 weeks (starting July that year). While Drake’s “Gently,” featuring Bad Bunny, held the crown for one week in late 2023. The song makes waves across Billboard’s charts, debuting at No. 44 on the all-genre Billboard Hot 100 and No. 103 on the Billboard Global 200, powered by 11.8 million global streams. It also launches at No. 1 on Hot Latin Rhythm Songs and No. 17 on Latin Rhythm Airplay. Back on Hot Latin Songs, Spanish newcomers Judeline and Rusowsky crash the top 10 with their first Billboard-charting entry, the co-billed “BbY WOW,” with Karol G. It opens at No. 5 with 4.5 million U.S. streams — the highest debut by a Latin act on the current chart. “When Karol first reached out and asked me to write for the album, I was in the middle of my first arena run, so everything already felt a little surreal,” Lara Fernández Castrelo, known as Judeline, tells Billboard. “I ended up cowriting four songs, and as we worked together, I realized Karol and I were going through a very similar place emotionally.” Judeline also has writing credits on three other No Me Arrepiento tracks that landed on the chart: “Matadora” and “Te Llevas To” at Nos. 4 and 6, respectively, while “Final Feliz” debuted at No. 14. “When I wrote ‘Final Feliz,’ I immediately felt like it was a song she had to sing,” Judeline adds. “Then she invited me to be part of ‘BbY WOW’ with Rusowsky, someone I’ve made music with for years, which made the whole experience even more special. title: Vikings Sign Guard Joshua Gray - vikings.com
content:
EAGAN, Minn. — The Vikings added to their offensive line group Wednesday with the announced signing of guard Joshua Gray. To create a spot on the roster, Minnesota terminated the contract of vested veteran defensive lineman Eric Johnson II, who is free to sign with another team. Gray initially signed with the Falcons in 2025 as an undrafted free agent. The former Oregon State standout spent last season on Atlanta's practice squad and was elevated to its active roster in Week 10. The Falcons waived Gray in July, and he signed with the Panthers in August. He played last week in Carolina's preseason game against Buffalo, playing 39 percent of the team's offensive snaps. Gray played his entire collegiate career (2019-24) at Oregon State, where he started a school-record 56 career games — including 44 consecutive starts from 2020-23. As a redshirt senior in 2024, Gray played 916 snaps, more than anyone else on the Beavers roster. He helped Oregon State's offense rush for an average of 189.2 yards per game and allowed just one sack. Gray, who was penalized just once, received a grade of 74.1 from analytics site Pro Football Focus for his 2024 campaign. Gray shares an alma mater with Vikings center Blake Brandel; the two overlapped at Oregon State in 2019. A California native, Gray attended Rancho Cucamonga High School and was a First-Team All-League and First-Team All-CIF selection. title: Goldman's LCN Deal Extends Its Push to Scale AWM & Durable Revenues - TradingView
content: In sync with the broader effort to scale Asset & Wealth Management (AWM) and increase the share of recurring, fee-based revenues in its earnings mix, The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. GS entered an agreement to acquire LCN Capital Partners. Over the past several years, Goldman has sought to reduce earnings volatility by expanding capital-light, fee-generating businesses and reducing the reliance on balance-sheet-intensive investing. The AWM business has become a key pillar of that strategy. According to the Goldman 2025 annual report, the company has doubled its more durable revenues since 2020 while reducing historical principal investments by more than 90%, from roughly $64 billion to $6 billion. title: BMW Spied Testing An All-New Middleweight Adventure Motorcycle - inkl
content:
We've been hot on the heels of BMW's many all-new upcoming bikes. Between an all-new M 1000 RS and a frankly bonkers R 20, I wasn't expecting to see much else from the Austrian brand this year. As usual, I was wrong. BMW was recently spotted testing what appears to be an all-new middleweight adventure bike. The bike looks like it'll sit between the current F 450 GS and F 900 GS, filling a very apparent gap in BMW's adventure lineup. With bikes like Yamaha's Ténéré 700 and KTM's 690 Adventure crushing it in this ever-popular category, it could prove a wise move for BMW to throw its hat in. The question is whether the manufacturer will have what it takes to compete with platforms that've been refined over a few generations. As is the case with these types of spy shots, we don't have a lot of info to go on, but in this instance there's plenty to speculate about. What looks pretty clear is that the chassis and braking system are based on the current F 900 GS, and it rolls on spoked rims, with a 21-inch tyre at the front and an 18-inch to the rear. We can also see that the prototype uses a steel bridge frame, which is very similar in design to that found on the F900 GS. Adventure enthusiasts will be happy to know that this bike is based on the capable F 800 GS's chassis, but there are still elements of the brand's entry-level F 450 GS on this all-new motorcycle, including the engine. It appears that this upcoming model might use a heavily reworked version of the powerplant found in the F 450 GS, but that shouldn't come as a surprise. BMW is partnered with TVS, which uses a heavily revised version of the F 450 GS's engine in the Norton Atlas. In the Atlas, that parallel twin puts out 70 hp, but it's unclear whether BMW will use an almost identical unit in this new model or change the displacement. In any case, all signs point to this being in and around 600 cc, leaving the question: will this be a BMW F 600 GS or will the brand revive the F 650 GS? I don't think we'll find out whether this model is set to become an F 600 GS or F 650 GS anytime soon, based on the unfinished bodywork. Rising confidence in boardrooms, steadier financing conditions, and a backlog of companies eager to raise money or change hands have combined to reopen windows that had been shut. Alex G's instrumental themes will be featured on the soundtrack, alongside "Pain is the Heart of Love," an original track he recorded with Paul Buchanan of the bygone Scottish band the Blue Nile. That song dropped last week ahead of the soundtrack's release on digital platforms this Friday. It features lyrics from "Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma" director Jane Schoenbrun, who also hired Alex G to score their previous two films, "We're All Going to the World's Fair" and "I Saw the TV Glow." Their latest soundtrack collaboration also includes music not by Alex G that appears in the film. Listeners can expect ample '90s pop and rock like R.E.M., Donna Lewis and Counting Crows. (After seeing the movie, you'll never hear "A Long December" the same way.) But a few post-2000 tracks made the cut. Sally Shapiro's Italo disco earworm "Anorak Christmas" and Andy Shauf's thematically appropriate "Satan" are on the album, too. title: BMW F 650 GS: tech, name and what to expect in 2028 - motorcycles.news
content:
BMW has had a gap between its small and large adventure bikes for years. At the bottom sits the F 450 GS, which replaced the G 310 GS at EICMA 2025. Above it come the F 800 GS and the F 900 GS with 895 cubic centimetres. In between there has been nothing at all. That gap is exactly where a motorcycle now photographed as a prototype on public roads appears to be aimed. The individual components can already be identified fairly precisely in the pictures. The prototype shows a slim adventure bike with a clear off-road focus. It runs a 21-inch wheel at the front and an 18-inch wheel at the rear, both cross-spoke wheels with tubeless tyres. Those wheel sizes are a clear signal. The smaller F 450 GS follows a different recipe, which puts the new middleweight GS closer to classic adventure bikes. The bodywork still looks rough and provisional, while individual design elements are already neatly finished. The headlight visibly picks up elements of the R 1300 GS. The typical GS beak above the front wheel is missing so far, which may simply be down to development still being under way. Observers reckon the generous ground clearance points to around 230 millimetres (roughly 9 inches) of suspension travel. One of the few figures on weight: the kerb weight is said to be around 204 kilograms (roughly 450 pounds), placing it between the F 450 GS and the F 900 GS. The engine is the most interesting and at the same time the least clear point. All that is certain is that it is a parallel twin showing visible technical kinship with the F 450 GS. A look at the United Kingdom helps here. BMW partner TVS, which builds the F 450 GS in India, uses a further developed version of this twin for the Norton brand. In the Atlas and the Atlas GT the heavily reworked unit delivers 585 cubic centimetres and 70 hp (51 kW). That very engine is regarded as a possible starting point. The picture is not entirely clear cut, though. In the photos the prototype’s engine differs from the British machine in several areas, while other areas look very similar. Some observers even assume that BMW is developing a completely separate unit that is based neither on the F 450 GS nor on the F 900 GS nor on the Norton twin. BMW has issued no official statement on either reading. This question is open and technically particularly interesting. The Norton twin works with a 270-degree firing interval, as is common in this class. The F 450 GS, by contrast, uses an unusual 135-degree crankpin offset. The firing interval describes the time gap between the two cylinders firing. It influences how the engine feels, how it sounds and how well the power can be metered off road. Whether BMW carries the idiosyncratic 135-degree solution over into the middleweight class or switches to the usual layout cannot be determined from the photos. Between 65 and 70 hp (48 to 52 kW) is expected. That range follows from the existing model line-up, because space is tight both below and above. The F 800 GS makes 87 hp (64 kW), the F 850 GS 95 hp (70 kW) and the F 900 GS 105 hp (77 kW). A new middleweight GS would have to sit clearly below those figures, otherwise it would take customers away from BMW’s own models. Some international estimates go a little further and consider up to 80 hp (59 kW) possible. None of these figures is confirmed; all of them are derived from the surrounding model range. With the chassis, the look goes upwards rather than downwards. The prototype’s steel bridge frame is oriented more towards the F 900 GS than towards the small F 450 GS. The brake system also resembles the larger range. In other places the kinship with the entry-level class remains visible. The mounting of the rear shock and the swingarm are reminiscent of the F 450 GS. The exhaust system and individual chassis parts also fall back on a similar recipe. The bottom line is a motorcycle that brings together components from several GS generations. The name is open, with three variants under discussion. F 600 GS would fit the current system, and a return of the F 650 GS or F 700 GS badges is equally conceivable. The name F 650 GS in particular would have a special ring to it for many riders. The F 650 GS Dakar from the early 2000s is still regarded as a benchmark for affordable adventure bikes with genuine off-road ambition. Reviving it would therefore also be a link to BMW’s own history. The actual displacement is unlikely to be a criterion for the name. The F 800 GS, the F 850 GS and the F 900 GS carry different numbers but share the same cylinder volume of 895 cubic centimetres. The Honda Transalp and the Yamaha Ténéré 700 apparently serve as benchmarks during testing. Both models define the middleweight adventure segment and are therefore the yardstick. The Japanese rivals come in at 755 and 689 cubic centimetres respectively. Should BMW indeed stay at around 585 cubic centimetres, the new GS would be the smallest machine in this comparison. The motorcycle is expected in India as well, where a price of around 1.2 million rupees (approximately 10,800 euros / 12,550 US dollars) is anticipated, placing it between the F 450 GS and the F 900 GS. That figure, however, is purely an estimate with no manufacturer information behind it. A production launch is not to be expected before 2028. The development stage of the prototype shows that considerable work still lies ahead of BMW. Plenty will happen in the model range before then. The F 450 GS is set to be joined by at least a naked bike at EICMA in autumn 2026, and presumably by a sports model as well. The middleweight GS would therefore only be the step after next on the new platform. It is also possible that the F 800 GS will drop out of the range once the new model arrives. That has not been confirmed. A production launch is not expected before 2028. The prototype that has been spotted is at an early stage of development and many design details are still missing. There is no official announcement from BMW so far. Between 65 and 70 hp (48 to 52 kW) is expected. That would place it clearly below the F 800 GS with 87 hp (64 kW) and the F 900 GS with 105 hp (77 kW). Some estimates also consider up to 80 hp (59 kW) possible. It is a parallel twin with visible kinship to the F 450 GS. The version reworked by TVS with 585 cubic centimetres and 70 hp (51 kW), used in the Norton models, is regarded as a possible starting point. Whether BMW adopts that unit or builds its own design remains open. The name has not been settled. F 600 GS, F 650 GS and F 700 GS are all being mentioned. The actual displacement plays no part in this, since BMW also uses different numbers for the F 800 GS, F 850 GS and F 900 GS despite an identical cylinder volume. The Honda Transalp and the Yamaha Ténéré 700 apparently serve as benchmarks during testing. Both are considered the standard in the middleweight adventure class and come in at 755 and 689 cubic centimetres respectively. Redakteur bei Motorrad Nachrichten. In 1990, USA Today formally contacted NASA to clarify rumors about their latest technology, apparently dubbed “sex packets.” Weeks prior, Oakland’s afrosurrealist rap collective Digital Underground (DU) had released their debut album, Sex Packets, themed around a new drug for astronauts that could instantly gratify their sexual desires. As DU’s transgressive lyrics glorified the illicit substance, news of the invention leaked onto the Bay Area’s streets: pamphlets were distributed, and condoms were passed out. NASA was forced to respond to the coital discourse: “NASA has not in the past, nor will they in the future, be working on such a pill … It would be impossible to satisfy the carnal urges of astronauts … To my knowledge, unbridled lust has never interfered with a space mission.” It’s the first and likely last instance of NASA being outmaneuvered by Oakland rappers. (It turned out DU had created the pamphlets and condoms as subversive promotional materials.) The elaborate prank was a piece of artistic genius orchestrated by Gregory Jacobs — the late MC, songwriter, illustrator, pianist and costume-wearing virtuoso known as Shock G. The NASA incident is just one of the many shenanigans detailed in his posthumous memoir, Keep It Beautiful: Inside the Funkyverse of Shock G and Digital Underground, out Aug. 25 — Shock G’s birthday — from Penguin Random House. The book combines handwritten notes, interview transcripts, personal photos and rare sketches compiled by Jacobs’ longtime friend and photographer, Alexis Wolfe Mbassa, who tagged along with Jacobs in order to document his eccentric life for over a decade. The association was intentional; in 2011, Jacobs personally recruited Wolfe Mbassa as a co-author for his autobiography. In 2021, just eight months after submitting the book to literary agents, Jacobs died from a drug overdose in Florida. He was 57. “It was never about money or becoming successful for him; it was about having the freedom to create,” Wolfe Mbassa told KQED. “He put himself in wild situations just to hold on to that freedom.” Wild situations form much of Keep It Beautiful. It details Jacobs’ stints in pimping, homelessness and jail, while containing all of the exuberant, out-of-pocket abundance of a Shock G production. A conversation between Shock G and George Clinton of Parliament Funkadelic? Yup. An African gray parrot named Afro who lives in Shock G’s childhood home and imitates his stepmom, Sonya? That too. One entire chapter is dedicated to his early friendship with a teenage Tupac Shakur, who joined DU as a member before going solo. (Apparently Pac had a “fucked” jump shot in basketball, and no one wanted him on their team). Largely stream-of-consciousness in homage to Jacobs’ creative process, the book is divided into sections based on the regions where he lived. Wolfe Mbassa traveled to each of them to conduct interviews: Topanga Canyon, Hollywood, Los Angeles, Oakland, New York City and Tampa. Jacobs recounts his first job as a 15-year-old, DJing at a local radio station in Tampa. He was fired for disobeying the radio’s directives and opting to spin the full 15-minute version of “(Not Just) Knee Deep” by Funkadelic instead of airing commercials. It isn’t the only example in the book of his natural inclination to rebel. Jacobs extensively details how he evaded authorities, and circumvented court appearances, from age 17 to 22. Even for the most studious hip-hop heads, Keep It Beautiful reveals overlooked wrinkles in Shock’s personality and biography. (Did you know that DU’s original band name was “Spice Regime”?) The book also includes a trove of never-before-seen drawings by Jacobs, showcasing a crude and whimsical style that would come to define his artistry, which sometimes reached ridiculous levels of raunch. (One sketch portrays an anthropomorphic anus forcing an “ASS-PIRIN” pill down its own hole.) But the main thrust of Keep It Beautiful are the granular narratives that Jacobs discloses, like his memories of being jailed in San Diego for six months for grand theft auto, where he used art as a bartering tool. In scattered, disconnected bursts, he and Wolfe Mbassa recount his side quests and failures (such as his brief time as a male “gigolo” in Pennsylvania) revealing the down-bad experiences that molded his worldview before his rap and art careers took off. Glimpses of that fast life can be heard in his lyrics, but the book shows in detail how Shock G actually did get around from coast to coast. At its core, the collage of archival material shows how music and art became Jacobs’ salvation, therapy and refuge. Putting it all together was a joyous challenge for Wolfe Mbassa, personally tasked by Jacobs to retain the book’s silliness and humor. “One of the most difficult parts was trying to figure out how to pull all the pieces together. He always wanted it to be like a scrapbook,” she says. “He wanted it to feel like his personal journals did: stories, mixed with memorabilia and art.” In sitting with Keep It Beautiful, its spiritual thesis is clear: Jacobs’ everlasting search for beauty, creativity and funky originality shone brightest during his darkest hours. It’s about keeping it beautiful, especially when beauty isn’t easily kept. “It was so much fun,” Wolfe Mbassa confirms, “to live in his world.” ‘Keep It Beautiful: Inside the Funkyverse of Shock G and Digital Underground’ will be released on Aug. 25. A free release party with Alexis Wolfe Mbassa and members of Digital Underground takes place Saturday, Aug. 22 at Drake’s Dealership (2325 Broadway, Oakland). Event information here.

Earlier this month, in the midst of touring her Tropicoqueta album, Colombian superstar Karol G unexpectedly released No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto, which translates to I Don’t Regret Feeling So Much. The title is an almost perfect thesis for the album: moody, raw, and unfiltered. There are melancholic ballads, including “Después de Ti,” her collaboration with Greg Gonzales of the pop band Cigarettes After Sex, alongside more unruly anthems like “Matadora,” or “Killer.” Fans had reason to suspect something new was coming. Months before the surprise album’s release, Karol began dropping beauty-related hints (unsurprising, as she’s someone known for playing with her hair colors and nails). In January, she posted a carousel on Instagram—including an image of herself wearing rhinestones across her forehead and a baby-blue manicure— captioned: “Unfocused But SparkLYYYY.” It was easy to write it off, as she was in the midst of building the world around her album Tropicoqueta. And in April, at the end of her historic Coachella set, Karol announced she was taking Tropicoqueta on the road. The resulting tour, Viajando Por El Mundo—or Traveling Around the World—seemed poised to continue the same visual language: flowers, fiery colors, and plenty of tropical extravagance. The cover art for “No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto.” But there was another clue for both her new album and “sentimental-blue” era. In one of the promotional videos for the tour, Karol opens a suitcase. Sparkles spill out. She looks at them and says, “No, I’m not packing that one yet.” It was a blink-and-you-miss-it moment, but it now feels like a preview of what was coming. The aesthetic of No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto could hardly be more different from Tropicoqueta. One is fluorescent, maximalist, and celebratory; the other is somber, introspective, and stripped back. On the album cover, Karol appears almost makeup-free and bathed in a cool blue hue—giving the image a nostalgic vibe reminiscent of Britney Spears 2003 album, In The Zone. For Karol, color has always been part of the storytelling, according to Duván Foronda, her makeup artist of nearly a decade. “She is someone who puts color to everything; for her, a song has a color; for her, a feeling has a color.” When they were creating Tropicoqueta, that feeling was happiness. “She said, ‘I want an album that’s really tropical, that feels really happy.’ And to her, the color that expressed that was orange,” Foronda recounts. The beauty followed suit. “That album had a really defined aesthetic,” he says. “In terms of the makeup, we did a lot of red lips, brown lip liner, and orange tinted cheeks.” A close up of Karol G's makeup for her “Viajando Por El Mundo” tour. Now, he’s helping Karol strip things back. Duván, whom Karol affectionately calls “Duvi,” has been part of the process of bringing the singer closer to a more natural version of herself. It’s an interesting evolution for an artist whose beauty identity has always been playful. Before joining Karol’s world, Foronda followed in the footsteps of his mother, Adriana Pérez, a notable Colombian makeup artist. He assisted her on various jobs until eventually building a career of his own, including working with lingerie brand Leonisa—comparable to Victoria’s Secret— which is one of Colombia’s most recognizable brands. There’s something fitting about Karol entrusting this particular beauty transformation to someone who understands the visual language of Colombian beauty from the inside out. For this era, though, the inspiration came from somewhere else entirely: Hawaii. During the trip, Foronda noticed Karol gravitating toward blue. “I noticed she started wearing a lot of blue,” he says. Eventually, she told Foronda why. “She told me, ‘I don't know, this new era, which is more mine, more vulnerable, more personal, feels blue.’” Soon, the color began appearing everywhere. “We would go out with her, and she would wear a blue shirt, sometimes a blue purse, or even a blue phone case,” Foronda recalls. But this isn’t an electric cobalt or the kind of neon blue that might have felt at home in the Tropicoqueta universe. It’s softer, airier. “You’ll notice it's not a vibrant blue; it's like a sky-blue,” he says. “It’s calming.” Karol performing in Los Angeles for her “Viajando Por El Mundo” tour. That sense of calm is starting to make its way onto the stage, too. On her Viajando Por El Mundo tour, which recently stopped in Los Angeles for three sold-out shows with special guests including Becky G and Bruno Mars, the energy of this newer era exists alongside the tropical spectacle that fans have gotten to know. “In the show, we’re still doing the Tropicoqueta [aesthetic], but we’re starting to add some new touches,” Foronda says. “We’re adding Swarovski crystals in her makeup, adding glitter to her makeup, and we’re also doing darker makeup.” It’s the “moodier” makeup, however, that is the biggest departure for the Colombian singer, says Foronda. “In this new era, we’ll see her with makeup that’s darker, riskier,” he explains. The deeper, more undone looks are meant to reveal another side of Karol: the rebellious one. The key to this look is a smudgy eyeliner. “It has to be messy; it can’t be glam or perfect, like a perfect line,” says Foronda. And if that feels like a rejection of the pristine, hyper-polished beauty which has dominated our feeds for years, that’s because it is— at least a little bit. After spending recent years embracing her natural beauty and the soft-focus appeal of “clean girl” makeup, Karol is embracing the mess. More eyeliner. More glitter. More crystals. More drama. The clean girls, it seems, are in fact getting glittery. Foronda’s inspiration board for this new direction is equally sparkly. “I get a lot of inspiration from Zara Larsson’s makeup artist, Sophia [Sinot],” he says. “I love all the glitter she uses, and the little rhinestones she adds to the eyes. I love all the glitter she adds to her body.” His technique is refreshingly low-tech. “I bought an [eyeshadow] palette, and I mix it with body lotion.” The eyeshadow palette is from a New Zealand-based brand, “Question Beauty” while a new MIM body lotion—Foronda’s makeup brand— inspired by a lyric in Karol’s song “Ivonny Bonita” is expected to launch soon and will be available worldwide. Bruno Mars joining Karol on-stage during her "Viajando Por El Mundo" tour in Los Angeles. Of course, underneath all that glitter is skincare. Before a show, skin prep takes priority. Foronda’s secret weapon is a 15-minute Medicube Booster Pro massage that provides temporary rejuvenating effects through LED, microcurrent, sonic vibration, and EMS (electric muscle stimulation), alongside the MIM Hydrating Gel, which contains hyaluronic acid and vitamin B5. Afterward, it’s all about removing what went on. According to Foronda, Karol swears by the MIM Gentle Makeup Remover, particularly when it comes to the layers of mascara required for a stage performance. “For a show, you have to wear a lot of makeup, and that includes heavy mascara,” he says. “And she would always [accidentally] take off all her eyelashes when taking off her makeup.” Now, the remover has become a permanent fixture in Karol’s kit. “She would tell me, ‘There’s no makeup remover like this one.” It’s a small detail, but it captures the beauty philosophy behind this new chapter: the drama can be taken off. The rhinestones can come off. The glitter can be washed away. What remains underneath is the person Karol has been trying to get closer to all along. title: GS Points Leaders Seek Bounce Back This Weekend at VIR - Sportscar365
content: With new co-driver, McCumbee McAleer Racing looking to return to form this weekend at VIR… The IMSA Michelin Pilot Challenge GS championship leaders look to rebound from abnormal Road America results for the Virginia Is For Racing Lovers Grand Prix at Virginia International Raceway. Robert Noaker will share the No. 13 McCumbee McAleer Racing Ford Mustang GT4 with new co-driver Finn Wiebelhaus starting at VIR. The No. 13 car has finished in the top 11 in each of the first seven races and built its championship lead from 30 points to 100 entering VIR. Ford scored a pair of podiums at VIR last year in the hands of KohR Motorsports, finishing second and third behind eventual season champions Luca Mars and Jan Heylen in the RS1 Porsche 718 GT4 RS CS. Each of the top five in the championship all finished seventh or worse in the Road America 120. That brought a sixth possible GS title contender into play, in the form of series newcomers YRB Racing and Road America winners Trenton Estep and Allen Patten in their No. 66 Aston Martin Vantage AMR GT4 Evo. The second consecutive first-time GS winners have ascended to sixth and only 190 points out of the lead. A second successive win would propel this team even closer to the front of the pack only a handful of races after debuting at Watkins Glen International following an acquisition of van der Steur Racing. But winning this season has not necessarily been a good thing for GS winners in their next race. In an odd quirk, the results for GS winners in their next race, starting at Sebring, have been 29th, ninth, second, fourth, 21st and 28th, for an average 15th place finish. The gap from first to 15th place in IMSA’s scoring system is, conveniently, 190 points. Mars and Dillon Machavern rebounded with a seventh place in their No. 95 Turner Motorsport BMW M4 GT4 EVO to jump back to second in points. They’re tied with fellow BMW runners Stevan McAleer and Austin Krainz in their No. 27 AutoTechnic Racing BMW and 10 points clear of fourth-placed Michael Cooper and Moisey Uretsky in the No. 44 Ibiza Farm Motorsport McLaren Artura GT4. Winward Racing’s Bryce Ward completes the top five, 160 back, in his No. 57 Mercedes-AMG GT GT4. TCR has, on paper, been a bit more straightforward. The Mason Filippi and Bryson Morris pair secured their sixth podium from seven 2026 starts aboard the No. 33 Bryan Herta Autosport Hyundai Elantra N TCR. They hold a 150-point lead on teammates Preston Brown and Denis Dupont, who share the No. 76 Hyundai. Either or both of these two need a big VIR result to make inroads on the Nos. 33 and 76 cars, which appear set to vie for the title in the last three races. Among the 42 cars split 29 GS and 13 TCR, there are several other changes. CarBahn’s No. 39 BMW is absent this race. CSM now switches to Aston Martin for its two entries, and its second car features Ismaeel Ellahi graduating from IMSA VP Racing SportsCar Challenge alongside Ayrton Houk. Kingpin Racing makes its second start of the season with Patrick Wilmot and Tyler Hoffman. Celso Neto and Eddie Gou, who finished second in TCR at Road America in the No. 55 Gou Racing w/Stallion Audi RS 3 LMS TCR, switch to the No. 77 Stallion Motorsports w/GOU CUPRA Leon VZ TCR this race. There are two one-hour practice sessions Friday, with qualifying Saturday morning and the Saturday race at 2:15 p.m. ET and local time. title: No Regrets, Just No. 1s: Karol G’s ‘No Me Arrepiento De Sentir Tanto’ Debuts Atop Top Latin Albums Chart - Billboard
content: The singer claims her fifth leader on the tally and impacts the Hot Latin Songs chart. Sr. Charts & Data Analyst (Latin & Billboard Español) Karol G’s sixth studio album, No Me Arrepiento De Sentir Tanto, debuts at No. 1 on Billboard’s Top Latin Albums chart (dated Aug. 22), halting Bad Bunny’s reign with Debí Tirar Más Fotos, which has spent a record 77 nonconsecutive weeks atop the list and has been No. 1 since the Jan. 24-dated chart. Karol G’s set also floods Hot Latin Songs with 13 entries, led by “Ahí,” with Drake, which opens at No. 1. No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto was released Aug. 7 via Bichota/Interscope/Capitol, just more than a year after Tropicoqueta led the Top Latin Albums chart for two weeks in July 2025. The new set marks Karol G’s fifth straight debut at the summit among seven career entries — only Unstoppable and Ocean fell short, peaking at No. 2 in 2017 and 2019, respectively. No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto begins with 50,000 equivalent album units earned in the United States in the tracking week of Aug. 7-13, according to Luminate. For its chart debut, the set registered 48,000 from streaming activity, which equals to 49.5 million official on-demand streams. Album sales comprised a little over 1,000 units, with a negligible number of track-equivalent units. With No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto, Karol G adds her fifth No. 1 on Top Latin Albums. No other female artist has dominated the overall Latin albums ranking in the past decade like Karol G, who trails only the late Jenni Rivera and Shakira, each with seven No. 1 albums, the most among female artists in the chart’s history, dating to 1993. Meanwhile, No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto opens at No. 8 on the all-genre Billboard 200 — Karol G’s fourth top 10 — and breaks through to No. 1 on Top Latin Pop Albums. Plus, the set arrives at No. 7 on Top Streaming Albums. Here’s a rundown of Karol G’s No. 1s on Top Latin Albums: On the tracks front, 13 tracks from the new album join two already charting titles on Hot Latin Songs, which includes streaming data, radio airplay and digital sales into its formula. “Después de Ti,” with duet parter Greg González, and the album’s first charting track, flies 17-10, while fellow advance single “Matadora” slips 4-3. But the biggest winner is “Ahí,” her collab with Drake, which debuts at No. 1 largely by 5.9 million official U.S. clicks. The sum yields a No. 46 start on the overall Streaming Songs chart, and a No. 1 on Latin Streaming Songs. title: Lunchbreak: Blake Cashman's Impact Stretches Through Vikings Defense; Rookie Report Card - vikings.com
content:
We're getting to the point in training camp — and of Blake Cashman's ascension in Minnesota — where our eyes are playing tricks on us. Basically, we're taking for granted his steadiness and sheer dominance. Perhaps, it's the way he teleports to the quarterback on blitzes. Or his wherewithal in coverage. Or his presence in the middle that feels so large and in charge, and natural, that it's like he's been here forever. Technically, Cashman, an Eden Prairie native and former Gophers standout, has been nearby most of his life. The Vikings have only been spoiled by his talents — escalated by Brian Flores — since 2024, though. Andrew Krammer of the Star Tribune this week spotlighted the Vikings 30-year-old linebacker as he prepares to be the Commander-in-Chief of the defense, again, in Year 3 with his hometown franchise. The gist of the article is Cash’ is a coach on the field, and wants to be with Minnesota until he retires. Krammer recalled a sequence in practice on Aug. 7 when Cashman and second-year defensive lineman Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins busted into the backfield for what would have been a sack of Kyler Murray. It was a defensive highlight — no doubt — but Cashman's immediate reaction was to grab Ingram-Dawkins for a teaching moment. Ingram-Dawkins noted that Cashman was "telling me to be alert for certain things and stay on point." View photos of Vikings players during Training Camp practice on August 17 at TCO Performance Center. Krammer used it as an example of Cashman's value to the defense that eclipses a play's three-to-six seconds. It's particularly noteworthy because Cashman is entering the final year of his contract. "I love being here as a Minnesota Viking," Cashman told Krammer. "I don't want to be anywhere else." "But, of course, I'm at a point in my career where I'm honest," he continued. "I've got less time ahead than I do behind me. But I think I still have gas in the tank, and I want to hopefully finish my career here." Cashman has totaled 256 tackles over 27 starts with the Purple. Both tallies dwarf the number of tackles (181) and starts (21) that he made from 2019-23 when injuries limited him to 44 games and crushed his potential. Now, Cashman explained to Krammer, his legs are better off because of those early absences. And the Vikings have been well off with Cashman serving as the Green Dot. We highlighted the preseason debuts of a handful of Vikings on the ground in East Rutherford, New Jersey. A couple of days removed from the initial action of many young players' careers, NFL.com's Chad Reuter went a step further and attached a letter grade to one rookie performance in each of the 16 exhibitions. For Minnesota, Reuter went with the biggest draw, assessing first-round selection Caleb Banks. Reuter awarded the 6-foot-6, 327-pound defensive lineman a B-minus and wrote the following: Banks showcased his elite size and explosiveness off the snap in the first half of the Vikings win over the Giants. When attacking a gap, the No. 18 overall pick twice found the backfield, first forcing a nifty cut from Cam Skattebo and then [converging on] Devin Singletary. Banks thought he stopped a fourth-and-1 QB sneak in the second quarter, but a questionable spot gave New York the first down. On the next play, he stayed engaged with his blocker with one eye on the ball to make a run stop 6 yards downfield. Banks was moved off the line by single- and double-team blocks when he failed to maintain a low pad level. In the locker room afterward, Banks informed the media that he's focused on playing with better leverage, as well as sticking to his techniques and assignments. He played with "happy feet" on occasion, he said, and shared he was nervous for his first action (and only his fourth game since 2024 at Florida). Banks played 27 snaps and was credited with three tackles. All in all, Reuter's analysis captured the good and not so of Banks' debut, and future excitement for him. Reuter, so you know, distributed A-minus or better grades to three players: San Francisco WR De'Zhaun Stribling (A-), Los Angeles Rams QB Ty Simpson (A) and Jacksonville OL Emmanuel Pregnon (A-). title: Biz Buzz: St. G’s Bodega moving into old hardware store in St. Cloud's East End - St. Cloud Live
content:
ST. CLOUD — A new bodega store, St. G’s Bodega, is scheduled to open in early September on the site of an old hardware store in St. Cloud’s East End. It’ll have staple grocery items with a “New York bodega style,” St. G’s Bodega co-owner Maddie Waseka said. That means sodas, cereals, chips, cigarettes and more will all be for sale. “We wanted to add something that was a little bit higher-end than your standard grocery in looks and offered the everyday staples that people need on that side of town,” Waseka said. The location is 415 E St. Germain St., originally the old Sentinel Hardware building before it was purchased by Marla Waseka, Maddie’s mother, in 2022. The Waseka family, through their real estate restoration company, MoXie Ladies, has for years been purchasing dilapidated real estate on 
    
      St. Cloud’s East End,
    
       or areas centered around East St. Germain Street and the Lincoln Avenue corridors, east of the Mississippi River. The long-closed hardware store now houses 
    
      Respect Fight Club
    
       gym in the basement, breakfast and lunch restaurant 
    
      Kitchenette,
    
       home goods store 
    
      Sage & Salvage,
    
       four apartments and now St. G’s Bodega. Nearby, they also purchased the former Ace Bar building on June 26 with plans to restore it as a bar and restaurant. “It's more of a passion project than anything,” Maddie Waseka said. “We figure if we keep doing our own thing and put cool things in, people will come along behind us and do their own cool things on the East Side.” The St. Cloud Retired and Senior Volunteering Program is receiving a $425,000 continuation grant as part of AmeriCorps’ grant competition for organizations that offer volunteer opportunities for people 55 and older. RSVP
    
       is an AmeriCorps program dedicated to seniors hosted by the City of St. Cloud that serves Benton, Sherburne, Stearns and Wright counties. The program matches seniors with volunteer opportunities that match their interests, skills and schedules. The organization’s 1,200 volunteers have worked alongside more than 160 partner nonprofits, government agencies and healthcare groups. “We’re thrilled to be able to continue serving our communities,” RSVP Director Jennifer Wucherer said in a statement. “We are passionate about working with older adults — not only to help meet community needs, but also to honor and value the experience, knowledge and impact that older adults bring. Service is one of the greatest gifts we can offer and one of the more reliable ways to enrich our own well-being.” Around 130 grants were handed out nationally in 2026, with St. Cloud being one of five organizations in Minnesota to receive the award. St. Cloud Financial Credit Union Executive Vice President Chase Larson, who is also the company’s chief lending officer, is the newest member of the Central Minnesota Habitat for Humanity’s board of directors. The board is responsible for ensuring good financial stewardship and accountability. Chad Bouley, executive director for the local branch, said Larson brings sound business leadership to the organization. “Chase is a proven leader in our community, and his vision, creativity, and passion for serving others will be tremendous assets as we continue to grow our impact. We are excited to have him helping shape the future of our organization and advancing our mission throughout Central Minnesota,” Bouley said in a statement. Central Minnesota Habitat for Humanity and St. Cloud Financial Credit Union have partnered on projects before. Central Minnesota Habitat for Humanity named SCFCU as its 2024 Business Partner of the Year. St. Cloud State University recently won a $135,000 state grant to partner with local machining manufacturer Park Industries to boost workforce development training. That figure rises even higher thanks to an additional $262,000 in matching funds from Park Industries to St. Cloud State’s Professional and Continuing Education (PACE) division. The two-year project will involve customized training, leadership development and digital skills training for 217 employees. The grant supports a "robust" training model designed to address workforce challenges in advanced manufacturing, including skills gaps, leadership readiness, digital transformation and employee retention in a tight labor market. The training initiative is expected to deliver measurable outcomes for both employees and the regional economy. This partnership reflects a shared commitment to building a resilient, inclusive and future-ready workforce across Central Minnesota, according to participants. PACE specializes in building employer partnerships that strengthen regional economies and create long-term talent pipelines. Visit the 
    
      PACE website

title: St. G's Bodega Opens On East St. Germain Street Just In Time For FestFall - WJON
content: ST. CLOUD (WJON News) -- A new place to grab some snacks and other essentials is coming to St. Cloud's East End. Marla Waseka owns the building and will operate the community grocery store with her two daughters. The term Bodega is common in urban places like New York City and basically means a small family-owned store or neighborhood convenience shop. It's kind of a gathering space for the neighborhood.  People are welcome to post neighborhood events that are going on.  It's going to provide some basic grocery items, personal care, and household items. She says they want the store to change and evolve as they get feedback from customers and neighbors. What we are creating here is an urban village, which is a place where everything is provided for the residents in the neighborhood.  There are services for them; there are shops, restaurants, and bars.  So eventually we could become a little self-sufficient neighborhood of our own. St. G's Bodega will have four tables and chairs in the front by the windows for people to sit and gather. Eventually they'll offer some prepacked sandwiches and other grab-and-go foods, lunches, etc. The Old Dutch Maid Bakery awning may also be brought out of storage and repurposed in some way in the bread aisle. Waseka says she plans to keep the vibe of a 1920s-era grocery store feel. The St. Cloud City Council approved their tobacco license on Monday night. Maddie Waseka opened The Kitchentte next door to St. G's Bodega a year ago on Festi-Fall weekend. Earlier this year, Marla Waseka bought the former Ace Bar building with plans to renovate that and reopen it as a bar and restaurant in the next few years. title: All of Karol G’s Albums, Ranked - Yahoo
content: If her debut album title is any indication, Karol G is truly "unstoppable." Maluma, Quevedo, Bebeshito & More Set for Billboard Latin Music Week 2026 Calle 24 Cancels Remaining U.S. Eterno Tour Dates After Work Visa Revocation: 'It's Out of My Hands' What Do We Make Of Karol G's 'No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto' Top 10 Debut? Her 2017 set, which includes collaborations with Ozuna on "Hello" and Bad Bunny on "Ahora Me Llama," instantly placed the Colombian artist on the map as one of the rising woman voices in reggaetón. By her third studio album, KG0516, which became her first No. 1 on the Top Latin Albums chart in 2021, she was a household name. And with her 2023 blockbuster Mañana Será Bonito, she had become a global force to be reckoned with. The latter made history on the Billboard 200 albums chart as the first No. 1 all-Spanish-language album by a woman artist, and won the coveted album of the year award at the 2023 Latin Grammys. Born Carolina Giraldo Navarro, Karol has released seven official studio albums from her 2017 Unstoppable to her most recent, No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto, out this month. While she's one to effortlessly experiment with new sounds, such as merengue ("Si Antes Te Hubiera Conocido"), dembow ("Ojos Ferrari"), bachata ("Amiga Mía") and Mexican music ("200 Copas), Karol's discography has truly captured all of her versions — vulnerable, in love, heartbroken and empowered — throughout the years. That precise evolution is represented in her latest set, No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto — a 14-track project where she's in her feels, mainly powered by nostalgic ballads. NMADST — a sonic steer from her 2025 tropical-heavy album Tropicoqueta — debuted at No. 1 on the Top Latin Albums chart and No. 8 on the Billboard 200 chart. Meanwhile, the new album's Drake-assisted "Ahí" debuted atop Hot Latin Songs, breaking Bad Bunny's record-holding streak with "DTMF." Below, Billboard ranks all of Karol G's albums, in descending order: Release Date: October 27, 2017On Top Latin Albums: Peaked at No. 2On Billboard 200: Peaked at No. 192 On her debut studio album, her first under Universal Music Latino, Karol G dropped some timeless gems including "A Ella," "Casi Nada," and the Bad Bunny-assisted "Ahora Me Llama," which also has a remix with Quavo. In 2017, the reggaetón-pop set became the highest-charting debut set by a woman in more than two years on Top Latin Albums chart, following Chiquis' Ahora that opened at No. 1 on the chart dated June 20, 2015. Release Date: August 7, 2026On Top Latin Albums: Peaked at No. 1On Billboard 200: Peaked at No. 8 Karol G poured all of her feelings into her newest studio album that fittingly translates to "I don't regret feeling so much." The 14-track production finds the Colombian artist embracing her emotions like never before, and for the most part, it's powered by melancholic ballads. Despite introducing her "sad Bichota season," the album also has some signature reggaetón and dance numbers, such as "Matadora" and "BbY WOW," the latter of which is in collaboration with Judeline and rusowksy and has quickly become a fan favorite on social media. The set is also home to Karol's first-ever collabs with both Drake on "Ahí" and Bruno Mars on "Still." Release Date: June 20, 2025On Top Latin Albums: Peaked at No. 1On Billboard 200: Peaked at No. 3 More than just a tropical-leaning album, Tropicoqueta is reflective of Karol's upbringing in Colombia. "This album is an homage to all those Latin music genres I grew up listening to," she previously told Billboard Español. title: State Department Expands Schedule Policy/Career Push as Other Agencies Could Follow - fedmanager.com
content: The State Department is reportedly expanding its push to classify more workers into the new Schedule Policy/Career category. According to GovExec, that includes expanding the search to identify more employees in the General Schedule (GS) 13 and GS-14 levels for possible conversion. The move is raising concerns among federal worker groups that other agencies could follow the State Department's approach. This comes after President Trump signed an executive order in June that reclassified approximately 8,000 employees into Schedule P/C, short of the 50,000 or so positions who were projected to possibly move into Schedule P/C. The new category reduces some of the traditional civil service protections available to employees, including protections related to adverse personnel actions. According to one State Department employee who spoke to GovExec, human resources officials at the State Department are “using a short questionnaire to determine if GS-13 and GS-14 level employees are working in policymaking positions that should be reclassified to Schedule P/C.” The questionnaire reportedly includes questions on whether a particular position formulates policy, develops regulations, provides substantive advocacy of foreign policy, represents the department before Congress, as well as other questions. The push to convert more GS-13 and GS-14 employees comes after a senior administration official said that 97 percent of employees converted so far are at GS-15 or higher. The official said a “small number” of GS-13 and GS-14 employees were also converted, but that most of them work at the Office of Management and Budget (OMB). A second staffer told GovExec that while the work is in the early stages, it’s moving “relatively fast.” OPM says the creation of the new category is necessary to ensure that federal employees holding policy making or policy influencing positions “can be held accountable for poor performance or misconduct. “ The creation of Schedule Policy/Career also remains the subject of legal challenges brought by groups including the American Federation of Government Employees (AFGE), Democracy Forward, and others.

title: JPM, GS, MS Stocks Edge Higher After-Hours — Banks Lift Dividends And Announce Buybacks After Fed Stress Test - Stocktwits
content: Shares of JPMorgan Chase & Co (JPM), Morgan Stanley (MS) and Goldman Sachs (GS) edged higher in after-hours trading on Wednesday after the banks announced higher dividends and buybacks following the Federal Reserve’s stress test, which showed the banking sector remains well positioned to withstand a severe economic downturn. At the time of writing, JPM stock was up 0.6% after-hours after closing the regular session down 0.21%, while MS shares gained 0.4% and GS stock was up 0.1%. JPMorgan Chase & Co announced a $50-billion share repurchase program and raised its quarterly dividend as part of updated shareholder return plans. The bank said its board also intends to increase its quarterly dividend 10% to $1.65 per share, up from $1.50 per share, for the third quarter of 2026. The new buyback program will take effect from July 1, alongside the updated shareholder return plans. Jamie Dimon, Chairman and CEO of JPMorgan Chase, said, “The Board’s intended dividend increase is supported by our consistent investment in our business and strong financial performance. The new share repurchase program provides us with the flexibility to deploy capital in ways that enhance shareholder value over time.” Goldman Sachs (GS) also increased its quarterly dividend by 11% to $5 per share from $4.50, pointing to strong earnings momentum and a robust capital position. The revised payout implies an annual dividend of $20 and will take effect on July 1, pending board approval. Morgan Stanley (MS) similarly announced a 15% hike in its quarterly dividend to $1.15 per share from $1. In addition, the firm said its board has reauthorized a multi-year share repurchase program of up to $20 billion, with no fixed end date, set to begin in the third quarter. The announcement by JPMorgan Chase & Co comes after the U.S. Federal Reserve released the results of its annual stress test. It showed that large banks are well positioned to withstand a severe recession and continue lending to households and businesses. The Fed said that despite more than $708 billion in total loan losses under the hypothetical scenario, aggregate capital declined only 1.6 percentage points and remained above minimum requirements. It added that all 32 banks tested stayed above their minimum common equity tier 1 capital requirements under a scenario that included a severe global recession, a 39% drop in commercial real estate prices, a 30% fall in house prices and an unemployment rate peaking at 10%. title: Could this be the new BMW F 650 GS? - Bike Rider Magazine
content: BMW Motorrad appears to be developing a new middleweight adventure motorcycle that could slot between the F 450 GS and F 800 GS in its global line-up. A test prototype has now been spotted, revealing several similarities to BMW’s existing GS models, although the final production specification remains unclear. The prototype appears to use a parallel-twin engine and shares some technical elements with the recently introduced F 450 GS. However, its chassis and braking components appear closer to those used on BMW’s larger adventure motorcycles, including the F 800 GS and F 900 GS. The motorcycle also runs a 21-inch front and 18-inch rear wheel combination, pointing towards stronger off-road capability than the smaller F 450 GS. The engine is currently one of the biggest unanswered questions. BMW could potentially use a heavily revised version of the parallel-twin platform found in the F 450 GS. BMW’s partner TVS already uses a significantly reworked version of this engine in the Norton Atlas, where its 585cc configuration produces 70bhp. It remains unclear whether BMW will use the same displacement or opt for a different configuration. Power could potentially sit in the 65bhp to 70bhp range, although the BMW is expected to have a stronger focus on off-road riding than the Norton Atlas. The prototype’s chassis provides some further clues about its intended role. It uses a steel bridge frame that appears more closely related to the F 900 GS than the F 450 GS, while the braking system also appears to have been derived from BMW’s larger GS models. Combined with the 21-inch front and 18-inch rear wheels, the setup suggests that genuine off-road ability will be an important part of the motorcycle’s character. The motorcycle is still in the early stages of development, with unfinished bodywork particularly noticeable around the front fairing. However, the headlight appears to feature an X-shaped design inspired by the larger R 1300 GS. Interestingly, the familiar GS beak is missing from the prototype. BMW has not yet revealed a name for the new adventure motorcycle. If the engine displacement ends up being close to 600cc, an F 600 GS name could make sense, while BMW could also revive the F 650 GS name previously used for its middleweight adventure models. Given the unfinished state of the prototype, development still appears to be some way from completion. A production version is therefore unlikely to arrive before 2028. If BMW does bring the motorcycle to market, it could eventually compete with models such as the Yamaha Ténéré 700 and the upcoming KTM 690 Rally. (GFUZ) made history on Monday, becoming the first pure-play nuclear fusion energy company to trade on a major public stock exchange. In an exclusive interview with Stocktwits, CEO Greg Twinney argued that fusion is not just a cleaner alternative to fission but is a fundamentally larger market opportunity. GFUZ stock surged 21% on its debut, added over 25% on Tuesday, and was trading about 2.5% lower in the overnight session. The Vancouver-based company, backed by Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, among others, went public through a SPAC merger with Spring Valley Acquisition Corp. III, which provided General Fusion with approximately $150 million in cash. Earlier, Twinney told the Wall Street Journal that the funding is sufficient to meet the scientific milestones required by its demonstration machine. The listing arrives at a pivotal moment. Surging electricity demand driven by the AI boom, the global spread of electrification, and the energy appetite of large-scale computing has renewed urgency around new sources of firm, clean power. Fusion has attracted growing investment and government attention as a potential long-term answer. According to the Financial Times, the number of private fusion companies has more than doubled over the past five years, intensifying competition at a time when the technology is still roughly a decade from commercialization. General Fusion is targeting its first commercial plant around 2035. Twinney's bull case for fusion starts with what it doesn't produce. Unlike fission, fusion does not generate long-lived radioactive waste, does not use fuels that could be weaponized, and carries no risk of a meltdown. "Fusion is just inherently safe. We're not needing to engineer safety into it in the same way that you need to with fission," he told Stocktwits. "When fusion fails, it kind of just fails safely and there's not really any fallout from that." That safety profile has a direct commercial implication: regulators around the world are moving to govern fusion "in a much lighter way" than conventional nuclear, Twinney said, which he believes creates the potential to site fusion plants closer to population centers and industrial demand. That's a significant advantage over fission, which requires remote, heavily secured facilities. "We get all the benefits that fission can provide without the downsides," he said. There's another significant advantage. Fusion reactors primarily use deuterium, which can be extracted from seawater and is "massively abundant." The other component, tritium, is rarer in nature but can be bred through the interaction of a neutron and lithium. Fission, by contrast, relies on uranium and other finite sources. "The overall market size because of the safety profile and the abundance of fuel in fusion is much bigger than fission," Twinney said. While advanced nuclear companies such as Oklo Inc. (OKLO) and NuScale Power Corp. (SMR) are often thought of as being closer to commercialization than fusion technology, Twinney said that the gap may not be as large as investors assume. While the road to commercialization for fusion technology has its challenges, including achieving reactor durability, tritium fuel breeding, economic viability, and the ability to efficiently extract and convert fusion energy into electricity, he argues small modular reactor (SMR) timelines also struggle with regulatory hurdles that can make timelines less predictable than they appear today. "I know that the timelines for SMRs, which can be very unpredictable due to regulations and those types of things, [are] probably not that different," he said. According to Twinney, the combination of abundant fuel supplies and a lighter regulatory framework could ultimately enable fusion to scale faster than conventional nuclear technologies once commercial viability has been demonstrated. However, Twinney does not view fusion and fission as mutually exclusive technologies. "They will be complementing each other," he said. "And I think that fusion kind of rounds out the nuclear circle if you think about it that way," he added. When asked about criticism from former Commonwealth Fusion Systems CTO Dan Brunner, who, in a recent interview with the Financial Times, said General Fusion's commercialization timeline was "very hard to believe," Twinney said the company’s timelines were based on real experimental results from its Lawson Machine 26. The machine is designed to demonstrate that plasma can be heated through mechanical compression rather than superconducting magnets or high-powered lasers, he said, adding that the company's early results validated the operating principles behind its MTF approach that are “not based on fiction or papers being written.” The timelines “are based on our real results from machines that we have built and operated and then eventually written papers on. But those are real results papers, not theoretical papers,” he said. Twinney also emphasized that General Fusion's approach could offer a cost advantage over many competing technologies. While many other fusion developers rely on expensive superconducting magnets, high-powered lasers, or advanced materials that have yet to be proven at commercial scale, General Fusion's Magnetized Target Fusion (MTF) system uses mechanical compression and a liquid-lithium wall that can protect reactor components from neutron damage, help with breeding tritium fuel, and absorbing fusion energy as heat that can be converted into electricity using conventional steam turbines. In an earlier interview with Stocktwits, Chief Strategy Officer Megan Wilson had also pointed to the economic advantages of MTF, which eliminate the need for expensive magnets, targets, lasers, or exotic, not-yet-invented materials. The technology also eliminates the need for frequent replacement of components damaged by neutron exposure, she had said. “Our plants are designed to be cost-competitive compared to coal, steam, and natural gas,” she had said then. “They are expected to deliver four times as much energy per unit of fuel as fission, without long-lived radioactive waste, positioning them as the superior nuclear technology for sustainable growth.” By avoiding costly magnets and lasers and using existing industrial technologies, Twinney said he believes General Fusion has a clearer path to building an economically viable power plant, as the company’s design has from the beginning aimed to avoid the major barriers to commercializing fusion. "What we are trying to do at General Fusion, and our power plant design from the beginning, has been we want to avoid the major barriers to commercializing fusion. Not just demonstrate a bunch of fusion, but actually avoid the barriers to commercializing it," he said. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around GFUZ stock is ‘bullish’ amid ‘high’ message volumes. title: The 300-HP Lexus Q-Ship Hiding A Bulletproof V8 Under Anonymous Sheetmetal - HotCars
content: By the late 1990s, Japanese brands had mastered the art of creating cars that were more than met the eye. Their European competitors were going big and bold, setting out their stall for what type of audience this car was going for. But Japanese luxury was more understated, quiet, and subtle. Sophisticated engineering, powerful engines, and surprising capability could all be hidden underneath more ordinary styling, creating a contrast between performance and appearance. But for those who knew, there was an exciting car underneath. By the late 1990s, Japanese automakers had spent years proving that they could match European manufacturers’ quality and technology. European brands like     Mercedes-Benz and BMW had built sportier models with reputations for aggressive styling and impressive performance — cars like the BMW E46 M3, E39 M5, or Mercedes-Benz E55 AMG — while Lexus instead focused more on subtlety, restraint, and a more anonymous aesthetic. This philosophy was very evident in the luxury sedan market. Where BMW and Mercedes-Benz's offerings would attract attention wherever they went, Lexus more commonly flew under the radar despite packing sophisticated engineering and, increasingly, powerful V8s under their hoods. It was a stark difference to their European counterparts, and helped to create something exciting: sleepers. Quiet confidence is what a sleeper is all about. It's knowing that you have far more power and capability than you let on, safe in the knowledge that you could deploy it whenever you wanted. And while European brands favored stylistic choices that announced their power, Lexus was comfortable obscuring theirs under unassuming bodywork and conservative exterior choices. In doing so, they created something far more interesting. For some, there’s always been something compelling about a car that hides its true potential. Something that doesn’t look as fast as it truly is. And during the late 1990s/early 2000s, cars were definitely trying to look every bit as quick as they were. Big wings, flared arches, and loud exhausts were the order of the day. But sleepers deliberately went in the opposite direction, blending into traffic and letting their performance do the talking. This was also a perfect option for executive, luxury sedans. Their restrained styling and business-like demeanor meant that a driver could have both comfort and power, should they want it, while the untrained eye would look over the car with no indication of what it was capable of. And while some brands opted for this method, it was Lexus that was arguably the best at it. The Japanese brand’s cars were never the showiest, nor the loudest, but the V8 engines they concealed gave them an intriguing personality. They were more than happy to provide refinement and elegance when required, while also quietly providing straight-line speed that would make many performance cars blush. And there was one car that did this with devastating efficiency. The first-generation GS, which was Lexus’ answer to the European executive sedan and was known as the Toyota Aristo in Japan, arrived in the early 1990s. Designed by Italdesign Giugiaro, it was a good if not particularly sporty alternative. The second generation refined the formula, improving on the chassis and bringing in the 430 nameplate, though the car remained somewhat easy to overlook in a crowded marketplace. But by the third generation, the car had come into its own. It started with the chassis. The S190 chassis used in the third-gen GS 430 was more rigid than its predecessor, had a more sophisticated suspension setup (using double-wishbones rather than the MacPherson struts), and allowed for a greater rear-wheel-drive balance. But the chassis was only part of the equation, and another crucial improvement came in the car’s engine. The 4.3-liter 3UZ-FE V8 provided 300 horsepower and 325 lb-ft of torque at a time when competing cars like the E39 BMW 540i made around 282 hp and 325 lb-ft. Power was, naturally, sent exclusively to the rear wheels, which gave it a decidedly more sporting edge than one might have expected. The car wasn't exactly a lightweight, coming in at over 3,700 pounds, but it could still hit 60 mph in 6.0 seconds en route to an electronically limited 155 mph. And it did all this while wearing the sheet metal of a sensible banker, rather than a dominating performance vehicle. The car’s aesthetic was one of what Lexus called “L-finesse”, or “Leading-Edge Finesse”. A corporate design philosophy, it aimed to turn Lexus cars from their traditionally understated designs into something far bolder and more modern. It prioritized simplicity, elegance, and a driver-first approach that tried to place controls in positions that were instinctive to the driver. The third-generation GS 430 was the first production car to employ this new take, with elements like the sloping roofline and stance aimed squarely at its European contemporaries. The wood veneer and touchscreens on the interior offered improved ergonomics to the driver, too, placing them at the center of the driving experience. It made for the     ultimate sleeper. People looking in their rearview mirror and seeing a GS 430 might presume that it wouldn't be able to keep up, but would soon be surprised as the unassuming sedan not only blasted past, but did so with its driver seated in luxurious comfort. But while the interior was good, it was the engine that was the real star of the show. Being a subsidiary of Toyota, the Lexus engineers didn’t need to reinvent the wheel when it came to powering the third-gen GS 430. They simply took one of the most proven engines in Toyota's arsenal — the 3UZ-FE — and deployed it with devastating efficiency. A naturally-aspirated V8, it came from the already-popular UZ lineup and had been popular in the LS 430. Its aluminum block helped to keep weight down, while dual overhead cams and Variable Valve Timing with Intelligence (VVT-i) allowed it to benefit from Toyota’s hard-earned reputation for reliability. Being NA also meant that power delivery was immediate and predictable, as there was no waiting for turbos to spool or superchargers to work after asking the throttle for more. This was important, because the car wasn’t designed to be a stripped-back performance machine: it was supposed to be ready to both cruise effortlessly between meetings and then eat up back roads, depending on what the day called for. That dual-purpose character was what the car was made for, and which made it the executive sedan sleeper icon it is today. The GS 430 never gained the mainstream success of cars like the BMW 5 Series or the Mercedes-Benz E-Class. And that’s arguably part of its charm. It’s a hidden gem among car enthusiasts, a V-8-powered monster without the additional drama. The car also laid the foundations for the continuation of Lexus’ V-8 GS lineage, and the L-Finesse philosophy. The GS 460 would iterate on what the GS 430 started, taking power up to 342 hp and adding an eight-speed automatic transmission compared to the GS 430's six. But the GS 430 was the one that started it. Today, the car remains an affordable, reliable, discreet option for those who know what they’re looking at. It’s not going to generate the most attention, but it’s not supposed to. It does the job, and it does it very well. We want to hear from you.
