title: New Midsize GS Spied: Is BMW Resurrecting The F650GS Dakar? - ADV Pulse
content: BMW Motorrad is working on a new midsize GS, recently spotted in prototype form. The move follows the launch of the F 450 GS at EICMA 2025, which replaced the G 310 GS and marked a fresh start for BMW’s entry‑level adventure lineup. Reports from Europe indicate BMW is benchmarking the new bike against Honda’s Transalp and Yamaha’s Ténéré 700, using both as development yardsticks. At the same time, BMW’s partner TVS — which builds the F 450 GS in India — already supplies a revised version of the parallel twin to Norton for its Atlas models. That engine comes in at 585 cc and produces 70 horsepower. The prototype GS seems to borrow some of that engine’s DNA, yet the Atlas has differences that raise questions about how BMW will configure the motor. One of the most notable distinctions lies in the crankshaft design. Norton’s twin uses the class‑standard 270‑degree firing order, while the F 450 GS runs with an unconventional 135‑degree crankpin offset. Whether BMW will carry that unusual setup into the midsize GS remains to be seen. As for output, expectations point to somewhere around 70 hp, keeping it below the F 900 GS’s 105 hp but right in the mix with other midsize adventure machines. Weight will likely slot in between the F 450 GS and F 900 GS at around 450 pounds wet. The chassis points to a steel bridge frame that looks closer to the F 900 GS than the entry‑level sibling, with braking components borrowed from larger models. Tubeless cross-spoke wheel sizes — 21 inches up front and 18 inches at the rear — reinforce its off‑road intent. Ample ground clearance also points to a longer-travel suspension in the 9-inch range. The bodywork still shows signs of early development, yet some design cues are already taking shape. The headlight appears inspired by the R1300 GS, though the trademark GS beak has not yet been added. The overall proportions and profile are reminiscent of the Yamaha Tenere 700, which is the model BMW is clearly aiming its sights at. Naming also remains unknown. “F 600 GS” would fit neatly into BMW’s current scheme, while reviving the “F 650 GS” badge is another possibility. For many riders, the idea of a modern take on the old F 650 GS Dakar from the early 2000s would add an extra layer of intrigue, which could be a way BMW might connect past heritage with its future midsize offering. And as history has shown, actual displacement may not be the deciding factor — past GS models like the F 800 and F 900 GS share the same displacement (895cc) despite their different names. It’s also possible BMW will remove the current F 800 GS from the lineup once this model is launched. What’s clear is that BMW still has plenty of work ahead. A production‑ready midsize GS isn’t expected before 2028, but the prototype signals BMW’s intent to strengthen its hand in one of the most competitive segments of the adventure market. title: Karol G 'marriage proposal': Her reaction made the moment even better - HOLA
content: Karol G has been collecting unforgettable fan moments on her latest tour, but a 56-year-old concertgoer may have just delivered one of the boldest yet. During the Colombian superstar's third Los Angeles concert at SoFi Stadium on Sunday, Aug. 16, a fan decided that seeing Karol G perform wasn't enough. He apparently came prepared to shoot his shot with a marriage proposal. The playful exchange was captured on video and shared across social media, including an Instagram Reel describing the concertgoer as a 56-year-old fan who proposed marriage to the singer. Other posts circulating the clip identified him as a "56-year-old Gringo fan" who described himself as "single and available."  And Karol G's reaction made the moment even better. The surprise proposal happened during the final night of Karol G's three-concert run at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California. SoFi Stadium's official schedule confirms that Karol G was booked for three consecutive shows on Aug. 14, 15 and 16 as part of her Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour, with the Aug. 16 performance beginning at 7 p.m. It was during that third show that the 56-year-old fan caught Karol G's attention. In clips circulating on Instagram, the concertgoer is identified as being 56 and "single and available," turning his interaction with the singer into what amounted to a very public dating application. The original Reel shared by entertainment account Desde La Curva describes the encounter as Karol G receiving a "propuesta de matrimonio," or marriage proposal, from the 56-year-old fan. Other accounts quickly picked up the moment, with one post declaring: "Un fan de 56 años le pidió matrimonio a Karol G en pleno show," meaning, "A 56-year-old fan asked Karol G to marry him in the middle of the show." This was not exactly a private candlelit proposal. Thousands of people were watching. Rather than brushing off the unexpected proposition, Karol G appeared amused by the exchange. The viral posts surrounding the moment emphasize the fan's declaration that he was "single and available," while footage and reposts show the singer engaging with him from the stage. Earlier this year, the 35-year-old singer discussed her relationship status and her thoughts on marriage and children following reports that she and Feid had ended their relationship. Karol G has also previously revealed that when it comes to an actual marriage proposal, the moment matters more to her than the ring. During a dating-themed interview, she was asked what she would do if a boyfriend proposed with a ring she hated. "I don't care," Karol G responded, explaining, "I care more about the moment when he asked me." As for her ideal proposal? "A really unique one," she said as reported by DailyMotion. "Be creative." Well, proposing from the audience of a packed SoFi Stadium certainly checks the "unique" box. Whether it checks any of the others is another question. The proposal is the latest in a growing collection of unpredictable interactions between Karol G and her fans during Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour. The tour officially began July 24 at Chicago's Soldier Field. During that opening concert, Karol G spotted another relationship-themed sign in the audience, this time from a pair of newlyweds. Their message read, "Nos casamos. Queremos ir a otro show de luna de miel," which translates to, "We got married. We want to go to another show for our honeymoon." Karol G didn't simply congratulate them. After asking where they wanted to go, the singer offered to send the couple to Paris to attend another Tropitour concert. "Nos vamos de luna de miel para París y a ver el show de Karol G," she told them, meaning they were going to Paris for their honeymoon and to see her show. The Los Angeles concerts have produced their own headline-making moments. The first SoFi Stadium show on Aug. 14 launched a three-night run, while the second featured a surprise appearance from Bruno Mars for the live debut of their collaboration "Still." © ¡HOLA! title: Locality Pay: Why A GS-13 In San Francisco Earns About $30,000 More Than "Rest Of U.S." - fedsmith.com
content: Subscribe to our free email list to get our news updates in your inbox. 2026 federal locality pay supplements range from 17.06% to 46.34%. See how it affects GS-13 salaries, high-3 averages, and annuities across top and bottom areas. Federal employees under the General Schedule receive a base salary plus a locality payment that varies by geographic area. The 2026 rates range from 17.06% in the Rest of U.S. locality pay area to 46.34% in the San Jose-San Francisco-Oakland, CA, locality pay area. The federal locality pay system adjusts General Schedule salaries to reflect differences in non-federal pay levels across geographic regions. Authorized by the Federal Employees Pay Comparability Act of 1990, the system took effect in January 1994. Its purpose is to reduce pay disparities between federal and non-federal workers performing similar work in the same labor market. Locality payments are calculated as a percentage of base pay and applied according to the employee’s official worksite. The Office of Personnel Management publishes annual tables that incorporate both the across-the-board base pay increase and the locality adjustment for each designated area. For 2026, locality pay percentages remain at the prior year’s levels, while base pay received a 1.0% across-the-board increase. A locality pay area is a geographic region where federal employees receive an additional percentage adjustment. The President’s Pay Agent defines these areas after receiving recommendations from the Federal Salary Council. The Bureau of Labor Statistics supplies the underlying data by comparing General Schedule pay with non-federal compensation at comparable work levels. The cost of living is not a direct factor in the calculations. Pay disparity between federal and non-federal salaries is the primary driver. As of 2026, there are still 58 locality pay areas, including separate areas for Alaska and Hawaii and the residual Rest of U.S. category. These percentage differences compound over time. Prior FedSmith reporting has shown how cumulative annual differences of even 2–3 percentage points can produce salary gaps exceeding $20,000 at mid-level grades within a five-to-seven-year span. The five-year cumulative column assumes the 2026 rates remain constant for illustration. Actual future rates will vary with annual adjustments, but the table demonstrates the scale of the ongoing differential. An employee in the San Jose-San Francisco-Oakland area receives nearly $30,000 more per year than a counterpart in the Rest of U.S. area at the identical grade and step. Over five years, that gap exceeds $149,000 before taxes or benefits. Because locality pay is added to base pay, employees in high-rate areas receive higher total compensation for the same grade and step. The system therefore produces clear winners and losers in absolute salary terms. Employees stationed in the San Francisco Bay Area or New York metropolitan region benefit from the largest adjustments. Those in the Rest of U.S. category, which still covers a sizable share of the workforce, receive the smallest supplements. The expansion of locality pay areas has narrowed the Rest of U.S. share over the past decade. New areas created in recent years moved thousands of employees out of the residual category and into higher-rate tables. Once an area is designated, subsequent annual adjustments continue to reflect local pay disparities measured by the Bureau of Labor Statistics. Locality pay counts as basic pay for several major benefits. According to Office of Personnel Management guidance on administering locality rates, the locality-adjusted rate is used to compute retirement deductions and benefits, life insurance premiums and benefits, premium pay, severance pay, and lump-sum payments for annual leave. This treatment means that employees in higher-locality areas contribute more to the Federal Employees Retirement System and the Civil Service Retirement System due to their higher salaries. They also receive correspondingly higher life insurance coverage under the Federal Employees’ Group Life Insurance program when coverage is tied to annual basic pay. The high-3 average salary used to calculate Federal Employees Retirement System and Civil Service Retirement System annuities includes locality pay. An employee’s three highest consecutive years of basic pay, including the applicable locality percentages, form the base for the annuity formula. Because locality rates differ by location, two employees with identical grades, steps, and years of service can retire with different monthly annuities solely because of the locality rates applied during their high-3 period. Using the 2026 GS-13, Step 5 figures, the average high-3 difference between the top-10 and bottom-10 locality areas is nearly $18,000. Under the standard Federal Employees Retirement System formula—1% of high-3 multiplied by years of service (or 1.1% for employees retiring at age 62 or later with 20 or more years)—that salary gap produces a permanent difference in the annual annuity, measured in thousands of dollars. The high-3 period is not required to be the final three years of service. If an employee worked earlier in a higher-locality area, those earlier years may form the high-3 if they produce a larger average. Conversely, transferring to a lower-locality area in the final years of a career can lock in a lower high-3 if the recent lower rates become the highest consecutive three-year average. Once the annuity is computed, the benefit is fixed and is not reduced if the retiree later moves to a lower-cost area. This means that locality pay flows directly into the high-3 average salary used to compute CSRS and FERS basic annuities. High-3 is the average of an employee’s highest three consecutive years of basic pay. For most GS employees, locality-adjusted basic pay is included. A career spent primarily in a high-percentage locality, or a late-career move into one, raises the final three years and produces a higher annuity for life. The reverse—moving to a lower-percentage area near retirement—can lower the high-3 if those years end up being the highest three. The location where an employee lives after retirement does not affect the already-computed annuity. Some employees, therefore, work in high-locality areas to maximize the high-3, then relocate to lower-cost areas. TSP contributions are also based on the higher basic pay, so higher locality pay can support larger retirement savings, though individual contribution rates and investment performance remain the primary drivers. The locality pay system continues to evolve through Federal Salary Council recommendations and presidential decisions on annual adjustments. For 2026, the published rates and area definitions remain the operative figures for salary determination, benefit calculations, and retirement planning. President Trump is expected to issue an Alternative Pay Plan for the 2027 pay rates before September 1. Presidents typically issue these plans late in the month. Expectations for a 2027 civilian pay raise remain low. A few months ago, the administration released its FY 2027 budget proposal. It had no mention of a raise for federal civilian employees. The Office of Management and Budget later confirmed that the proposal effectively calls for no pay increase. By contrast, the budget does include a military pay raise, described as follows: Pay Raise for the Troops. The Administration recognizes the importance of America’s warfighters and their families, so the Budget funds a military pay raise of seven percent for all DoD (Department of War) military personnel ranked E-5 and below, six percent for E-6 to O-3, and five percent for O-4 and above. This enduring investment, far above the standard annual military pay raise, builds on the President’s recruiting and retention success, by doubling down on the Administration’s goal to restore America’s fighting force. This mirrors last year’s process. The FY 2026 budget proposal also omitted a civilian raise. The subsequent alternative pay plan provided a 1% across-the-board increase and no locality pay increase for most employees (with higher adjustments for certain law enforcement personnel). A similar alternative pay plan is possible this year. If any civilian raise materializes—whether across-the-board only or with a locality component—it is likely to be relatively small. As of mid-August 2026, Congress has not advanced language that would override a low or zero civilian increase. Federal employees in locality pay areas will continue to earn more than those in the Rest of U.S. schedule. Wi-Fi Spec: BE18000Number of Antennas/Removable: 8/NoPorts: Input WAN – One 2.5 Gbps WAN; Seven 2.5Gbps LAN; USB 3.0 (Gen 1)Processor/Memory/Storage: Quad-core 2.0 GHz/2GB/256 MBWi-Fi chips: Broadcom BCM6766802.11be performance: 2.354 Gbps (at 15 feet)Range: 130 feetSize: 8.9 x 8.9 x 3.5 inchesEstimated Annual Electricity Cost: $27.13 At $400, Asus resets the bar for high performance gaming routers with its ROG Strix GS-BE18000. Its appearance may be plain Jane but the GS-BE18000 could be the year’s stealth gaming router with everything needed to battle the world on your terms. From top triband Wi-Fi 7 speeds to access to gaming accelerators to 8 networking ports, it separates itself from the rest of the best Wi-Fi 7 routers. Among the first to implement Automated Frequency Coordination (AFC), it features better speed, range and reliability than competitors. It doesn’t matter if you’re a Leaguer or Minecrafter, the ROG Strix GS-BE18000 is not only small and modestly priced but has the power to blast your gaming into another dimension. Read on to see if this is the best gaming router for your battlestation. With a list price of $450, it pays to shop around for the Asus ROG Strix GS-BE18000. It’s available at Best Buy for $400, making it an excellent bargain that can outperform and outplay routers selling for hundreds more. The slightly less powerful ROG Strix GS-BE12000 also sells for $350 at Walmart. Considering all the Asus ROG Strix GS-BE18000 can do, it is amazing that it is roughly the size of a shoe box at 8.9 x 8.9 x 3.4 inches. That’s less than one quarter the size of the company’s ROG Rapture GT-BE19000AI router with its eight antennas pointing every which way. Available only in black, the ROG Strix GS-BE18000 is anything but intimidating looking. In fact, its boxy appearance is high on the Meh scale and not what I expect when it comes to a fire-breathing gaming router. Still, it’s what’s inside that counts, starting with Broadcom’s BCM6766 Wi-Fi chip, a 2.0GHz quad-core processor, 2GB of RAM and 256MB of flash storage for the device’s firmware and settings. It lacks the dedicated AI hardware that graces the GT-BE19000AI router, though this 8-stream router takes advantage of 320MHz data channels, Multi-Link Operations (MLO) and 4K Quadrature Amplitude Modulation (QAM). Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips. It’s among the first to tap into the higher transmission power available through 6GHz Automated Frequency Coordination (AFC) for faster data speeds, longer range and higher reliability. Using AFC is rare today and only works in the U.S., Canada, U.K. and Saudi Arabia. Look for the circle to widen over time. Able to work on all three Wi-Fi 7 bands, the GS-BE18000 features 4X4 streaming for the 5.0 and 6.0GHz transmissions, while the 2.4 GHz band is limited to 2X2 action. It adds up to a throughput rating of 18.0 Gbps. All the router’s networking ports can handle 2.5 Gbps wired traffic. In addition to the input WAN port, the GS-BE18000 has a generous seven downstream LAN connections. There’s also a Gen 1 USB 3.0 port for running a print server, making the contents of a data drive active across the LAN or using a mobile phone as a backup Internet feed when your broadband goes south. In the back are buttons for using the Wi-Fi Protected Setup (WPS) for quickie client connections and turning the router on or off. It can run as a Wi-Fi router, wired access point or a wireless node in an AiMesh network. Its excellent Quality of Service protocol is integrated into the gaming features for top access to data. It may lack the GT-BE19000AI’s window to see its components inside, but the GS-BE18000 has the router’s key specs embossed on a raised strip. There’s no info screen although its LEDs light up the ROG logo in any of seven visual effects and choice of color. Its pattern doesn’t change when the router goes offline but the stack of four LEDs below has indicators for WAN, WiFi, LAN and Power. Passively cooled, the GS-BE18000 has innovative nanocarbon-coated aluminum heat sink fins to transfer heat away from the router’s sensitive electronic components. It draws room air in from the bottom and expels hot air from the sides and top and peaked at 103.7 degrees Fahrenheit. The router is secured by Asus’s AIProtection security software that includes ad blocking, web filtering and malware protection. It stands out from the crowd (including Netgear’s Armor) by being a no-fee service that includes continual updates to thwart the nastiest attacks. The three-year warranty and life of product support blow away the competition. The router’s support pages have the expected set up tips and firmware downloads, but the 32-page manual seems rudimentary if you print it. Meant for online use, it has dozens of internal links for set up and operation tips. Based on extensive testing using Keysight’s IxChariot networking benchmark and my HP Envy X360 notebook, the ROG Strix GS-BE18000 zoomed past competitors, making it an excellent online companion. With the software set to simulate 10 data hungry users and the router next to the test machine, the GS-BE18000 moved 2.238 Gbps of data over Wi-Fi and 4.465 Gbps over 15 feet of Cat 7 cabling. This puts it in the upper echelon of high-performance routers. At the real-world distance of 15 feet, the GS-BE18000 delivered 2.354 Gbps of live data, putting it between the TP-Link Archer BE770 at 2.181 Gbps and the Asus ROG Rapture GS-BE19000AI at 2.580 Gbps. It’s more than enough for those with multi-gig data plans. With the router and test system 50 feet apart, the GS-BE18000 dominated at 1.354 Gbps, ahead of the Archer BE770’s 1.239 Gbps and one-third more throughput than the GT-BE19000AI’s 1.006 Gbps. At 75 feet, its 900.8 Mbps topped the Archer BE770 (at 772.1 Mbps) and the GT-BE19000AI (528.3 Mbps). Its 40.9 Mbps reading at 90 feet was more mundane and beaten by the Archer BE770’s 70.9 Mbps and the GT-BE19000AI’s 49.1 Mbps. Its 100-foot range should satisfy those living in mid-sized homes but is off the Archer BE770’s 130 feet. Finally, the GS-BE18000 moved upwards of 1.309 Gbps to a room 25 feet away. That’s among the best and shows the device’s ability to efficiently fill a home with data. During my two weeks with the GS-BE18000, it showed itself to be reliable and fast, although it left a couple dead zones in the attic and basement. While in use, it consumed 17.7 watts of electricity for an annual estimated power bill of about $27.13 if it runs all day and night and you pay the national average of 17.5 cents per kilowatt hour of electricity. By contrast, the Archer BE770 was a power hog at about $36 a year. It took 5 minutes to set the ROG Strix GS-BE18000 up using the Asus Router app. After I plugged everything in, I needed to pick a picture of the router, although nothing in the interface matched. The closest was “WiFi routers” and the process was automatic. I added names and passwords. It can all be done through the router’s online interface at asusrouter.com Like other Asus routers, the app is where to customize its settings. The home screen shows the current LED lighting effect as well as links to the current speed, the Internet connection status and the gaming goodies. Below are tabs for Devices (number of online devices without tapping), Insight (for firmware updates) and Family (for Web filtering by age group). The Settings tab has everything from Diagnostics and Gaming to QOS and Wi-Fi details. The router’s browser interface’s main page is incredibly dense. In addition to the current traffic and IP addresses, there’s the LED lighting effects too. The ROG Strix GS-Be18000’s Game Mode not only shows the current latency specs and deviation, but packet loses along the way. It can be set as the top data dog in the house, making your gaming the priority. Diehard gamers will love the global Ping map. The game accelerators can speed up the action for seven online games. They range from World of Tanks to Diablo 3. If the economy’s overpriced and everything has got you down, the Asus ROG Strix GS-BE18000 is a genuine bargain that can move data as fast or faster than devices selling for much more. In addition to a generous eight 2.5 Gbps wired networking ports, the GS-BE18000 uses the latest Wi-Fi tricks to deliver more than 2 Gbps available over Wi-Fi and includes an excellent AFC implementation for increasing the power and reach of the 6GHz band At $400, it’s money well spent on filling a home with high-speed gaming data. I just wish it would menace my gaming friends more. Brian Nadel is a freelance writer and editor who specializes in technology reporting and reviewing. title: New BMW Middleweight Adventure Bike Spied Testing; Could Be the F 650 GS - BikeWale
content: Get Notifications on Latest UpdatesBMW Motorrad appears to be working on a new middleweight adventure motorcycle that could sit between the F 450 GS and F 800 GS in its global line-up. A test prototype of the motorcycle has been spotted, revealing several similarities to BMW’s existing GS models, although the production-specification details are still unclear. The motorcycle appears to use a parallel-twin engine and shares some technical elements with the recently introduced F 450 GS. However, its chassis and braking hardware are closer to BMW’s larger adventure motorcycles like the F 800 GS and the F 900 GS. The prototype rides on a 21-inch front and 18-inch rear wheel combination, suggesting it could offer stronger off-road capability. One of the biggest questions surrounding the motorcycle is its engine. Although it isn’t confirmed yet, BMW could use a heavily reworked version of the parallel-twin platform that powers the F 450 GS. BMW’s partner TVS uses a heavily revised version of this engine in the Norton Atlas, where the 585cc produces 70bhp. However, it remains unclear whether BMW’s motorcycle will use the same displacement or a different configuration. We expect a power output in the ballpark of 65bhp to 70bhp. That said, the BMW adventure bike will be a more off-road-focused model compared to the Norton Atlas. The prototype features a steel bridge frame that appears closer in design to the F 900 GS than the F 450 GS. Its braking system also appears to have been derived from the larger GS, while the 21-inch front and 18-inch rear wheels point towards genuine off-road capability. The motorcycle appears to be in the early development stage, with unfinished bodywork, especially around the fairing. That said, the X-style headlight seems to have taken inspiration from the BMW R 1300 GS, although the familiar GS beak is absent from the prototype. BMW has not revealed the motorcycle’s name. An F 600 GS nomenclature would fit if the engine displacement is around 600cc. However, BMW could also revive the F 650 GS name, which was previously used for its middleweight adventure motorcycles. Given the unfinished bodywork, the motorcycle seems to be at the nascent stage of development. As a result, a production version is likely to be launched sometime in 2028. When launched, this BMW adventure bike could rival the Yamaha Ténéré 700 and the upcoming KTM 690 Rally.

title: GS Global opens Houston office to target US energy projects - The Korea Herald
content:
Business GS Global opens Houston office to target US energy projects GS Global said Monday it has opened an office in Houston to expand its presence in the US energy and infrastructure markets. Located in Houston’s Uptown district, the office will target growing demand for project-based steel generated by increased investment in energy, power and infrastructure. GS Global previously managed most of its US business through its Los Angeles office. The company said the new base would help it respond more quickly to shifting market conditions, including stronger protectionism and global supply chain restructuring. The Houston office will seek and support steel orders for major projects while expanding the company’s role in the US energy value chain. It will also explore opportunities in chemicals, energy and shipbuilding equipment. GS Global plans to work with Korean steelmakers operating in the Houston area, including Hyundai Steel and Dongkuk Steel, while cultivating local engineering, procurement and construction companies and steel fabricators as customers. During the second half, the company will focus on building a local network and strengthening its project pipeline. From 2027, it plans to expand order support and pursue new businesses, positioning Houston as a key development hub for the southern US. “The Houston office is a strategic investment aimed at expanding our customer base and strengthening our sales competitiveness in the US,” a GS Global official said. “We will pursue opportunities beyond project-based steel to establish a sustainable foundation for growth in North America.” Trump says he will meet Kim Jong-un this year, puts N.
